title: What should Hermes call you?
help: A preferred name or nickname is enough.

title: What is the most useful job Hermes could do for you?
help: Describe the outcome that would make this worthwhile.

title: Are we planning a new Hermes installation or configuring an existing one?
help: The wizard records a setup plan. It does not install or change anything.

title: Where will Hermes run?
help: Choose the target operating system, not necessarily the device running this wizard.

title: Which machine or environment is the target?
help: Use a nickname or description. Keep host credentials and private network details out of this export.

title: What is already installed, and how can its version be checked?
help: Include the known Hermes version, install location or who can verify them. It is fine to leave this unresolved.

title: Which HERMES_HOME directory should this installation use?
help: Provide the intended path, or leave it unresolved until the target machine is inspected.

title: Which profile should be created or updated?
help: Use a profile name, or describe the existing profile to preserve. This does not rename or create it.

title: Which terminal execution environment should Hermes use?
help: Choose the intended isolation level; the deployment agent must verify supported backends.

title: What should the working directory be?
help: Give the intended workspace path and identify anything outside its scope.

title: What network access should tools be allowed?
help: This is an intended boundary, not enforcement.

title: Which destinations or network restrictions apply?
help: Describe allowed services and prohibited destinations; never include secrets in URLs.

title: Which model providers do you want to use?
help: Choose intended providers. Exact model availability, login methods and support must be checked against your installation.

title: What should the primary conversational model be?
help: Give the provider and exact model ID if known. A deployment agent must check availability before applying it.

title: What model should handle difficult reasoning?
help: Give a provider/model ID and when to use it, or explicitly say to use the primary model.

title: What model should handle quick or inexpensive tasks?
help: Give a provider/model ID and cost limits. Leave undecided routing unresolved.

title: What model should handle images or visual work?
help: Give a provider/model ID, or say that visual work is not needed.

title: Are there custom or local model endpoints?
help: Give a non-secret base URL only, or say none. Never include keys, tokens or URL passwords.

title: How should model access be authenticated?
help: Choose the intended method. Compatibility must be checked against the installed Hermes version.
options: API key supplied through environment variables

title: Which environment variable names will hold model credentials?
help: Names only, separated by spaces or commas, such as PROVIDER_API_KEY. Never paste values.

title: What spending and fallback rules should apply?
help: Describe budgets, provider restrictions and what should happen when a preferred model is unavailable.

title: What is the custom provider name and non-secret endpoint?
help: Also describe the expected API compatibility if you know it.

title: Which memory and knowledge services belong in the setup?
help: Built-in memory, external providers and knowledge sources are different things. These selections are setup intentions.

title: Which of those services already exist, and which need setting up?
help: Name each service and its current state. Do not include service credentials.

title: Where is authoritative knowledge, and what may Hermes read or update?
help: Describe the vaults, folders or other sources, read-only boundaries, and which source wins a conflict.

title: Which memory or search endpoints and provider names are intended?
help: Use service/provider names and non-secret URLs only. Provider compatibility must be verified.

title: Will you use an embedding service, and which one?
help: An embedding service is separate from the conversational model. Say none if it is not needed.

title: Which embedding model and endpoint should be used?
help: Give exact model ID and a non-secret endpoint if known. Leave unknown details unresolved.

title: Which environment variable names will hold memory-service credentials?
help: Names only, separated by spaces or commas. Never include values.

title: What may be retained, shared, corrected or deleted?
help: Describe privacy boundaries and how stale or conflicting memories should be handled. These rules still need implementation and verification.

title: Which external memory provider should be active?
help: Choose one intended provider. Built-in memory and knowledge-source skills are configured separately; support must be verified.

title: What is the external memory service endpoint?
help: Use a non-secret URL if applicable, or say provider-managed. Do not include URL passwords or tokens.

title: Should Obsidian be connected as a knowledge source?
help: Obsidian access is a knowledge-source capability, not an external memory provider.

title: Which Obsidian vault path is intended?
help: Give the path on the target machine if known. Writes still require the separately chosen boundaries.

title: How should built-in memory behave?
help: Describe whether user/profile memory is wanted, what writes need approval and any size limits. Do not copy private memories here.

title: Which search or index service should be used?
help: Choose the intended service category. The agent must verify installed search skills and service support.

title: Where is the selected search or index service?
help: Provide a service name and non-secret endpoint, or describe who can verify it.

title: Which channels should Hermes use?
help: Choosing a channel does not create a bot, send messages or grant access.

title: Which skills, tools or MCP services should be connected?
help: Name the capabilities you want, what already exists, and any prohibited actions.

title: What bots or separate profiles do you need?
help: Describe responsibilities, owners, channels and the context that must stay separate.

title: Which environment variable names will hold channel or tool credentials?
help: Names only, separated by spaces or commas. The deployment agent must provision values through an approved secure method.

title: Who should receive results and who reviews outgoing messages?
help: Use roles or nicknames, not private account IDs. Separate draft preparation from permission to send.

title: How should browser work run?
help: The deployment agent must verify the browser tool and selected user profile before use.

title: Which browser profile or service is intended?
help: Name the profile and allowed accounts or service endpoint; never include cookies, tokens or credentials.

title: How should MCP services connect?
help: Transport and authentication must match each actual service.
options: A mix of stdio and HTTP

title: Which MCP service commands or endpoints are intended?
help: Describe each service and allowed tools. This is reference text only; nothing will execute from this answer.

title: Which tools should be included or excluded for each service?
help: List the allowed scope, authentication owner and read-only restrictions where applicable.

title: Which recurring tasks belong in the initial setup?
help: Include cadence, timezone, delivery destination, failure behavior and when each task should stop. Say none if not needed.

title: What tests will prove this setup works?
help: Consider a model response, memory write/read, source retrieval, bot reply, approval boundary and recovery check.

title: What should be backed up before applying changes?
help: Identify the owner and recovery procedure. The handoff must verify the target installation before writing.

title: Where should the pre-change backup be stored?
help: Provide a target path or storage description and who controls restoration.

title: What should Hermes understand about your life right now?
help: Share useful context, not a biography. Leave out anything you want to keep private.

title: What values should guide the way Hermes helps you?
help: Describe a principle you want reflected in everyday decisions.

title: Which roles are you balancing?
help: For example, running a business, studying, parenting or caring for someone.

title: What would make this relationship easier to use?
help: You can describe reading, hearing, movement, attention or language preferences without explaining a diagnosis.

title: What personal context should remain outside this profile?
help: Describe categories or boundaries; do not include the private material itself.

title: How should Hermes feel to work with?
help: Choose the closest starting point. You can add your own description later.

title: How should Hermes challenge your thinking?
help: Disagreement should help you make better decisions. Choose your preferred approach.

title: What personality would make Hermes a good fit?
help: Describe the voice, energy and traits you want. Avoid assuming personality grants decision-making authority.

title: What assistant habits frustrate you?
help: Specific examples are useful: repeated questions, hype, vague claims or excessive detail.

title: How should Hermes communicate uncertainty?
help: Say when you want a best estimate, a source check, or a pause for clarification.

title: Where would you welcome initiative, and where should Hermes ask first?
help: Give concrete examples. This answer records your intent; it does not connect tools or enforce permissions.

title: Where would you like help?
help: These choices guide later questions. Selecting an area does not grant permission to act.

title: What active project should Hermes understand first?
help: Include the desired result, current stage, next milestone and anything blocking progress.

title: How will you know this relationship is working?
help: Name an observable result and a reasonable review point.

title: How should competing priorities be weighed?
help: Describe deadlines, commitments and what can wait.

title: What constraints should shape the work?
help: Include time, budget, dependencies or commitments without disclosing account details.

title: Which sources should Hermes treat as authoritative?
help: Name the files, people or systems that settle questions. Paths are optional; never include login details.

title: What should Hermes remember, and what should it avoid retaining?
help: These are requested handling rules, not a guarantee of storage or deletion enforcement.

title: How should Hermes handle old or conflicting information?
help: Describe which source wins, how conflicts should be shown and when to ask you.

title: What evidence do you expect from research?
help: Describe acceptable sources, citations, freshness and how facts should be separated from inference.

title: Which knowledge belongs to a project, a person or the whole team?
help: Set context boundaries without copying private records into the interview.

title: How should remembered information be reviewed or retired?
help: Say who can correct it, how changes should be recorded and when outdated context should stop being used.

title: Which kinds of tools might be useful?
help: This is a wish list, not a connection or access grant.

title: What actions need your explicit approval?
help: Name actions and limits in plain English. Do not enter passwords, keys, account numbers or approval secrets.

title: Which browser profile or accounts may be used, and for what?
help: Describe scope and off-limits areas. Do not supply credentials or session tokens.

title: Which files may Hermes read or change?
help: Name intended folders and read-only areas. Include any material that must never be accessed.

title: Who may be contacted, through which channel, and when must a draft be reviewed?
help: Use roles or nicknames rather than private contact details. A recorded preference does not send a message.

title: How should access be checked, limited and withdrawn?
help: Describe the owner of access decisions and what should happen when scope is unclear.

title: What kind of assistant team would you prefer?
help: This records a preference; no agents or model services are created.
options: A small set of independent specialists

title: What cost limits should guide model and tool use?
help: Give a budget or a rule for asking before paid work. It is fine to say this is undecided.

title: Which specialist roles would earn a permanent place?
help: Describe responsibilities and when a temporary helper would be enough.

title: How should work be routed between fast, inexpensive and more capable models?
help: Describe examples, escalation points and any providers you want excluded.

title: What context may a specialist or temporary helper receive?
help: Set limits on shared history, private sources and credentials. Do not include the secrets themselves.

title: What should a useful handoff contain?
help: Consider the task, evidence, decisions, unfinished work and who remains responsible.

title: When would regular help be useful?
help: Choose a starting rhythm. This does not schedule anything.

title: What timezone and quiet hours should be used?
help: Name a timezone explicitly if timed work matters. Leave uncertain timing unresolved.

title: Describe one recurring task worth automating.
help: Include its trigger, cadence, expected result and the actions that still need approval.

title: Where should recurring results be delivered?
help: Describe the destination and recipient by role or nickname; avoid private contact information.

title: What should happen when a routine fails or has nothing useful to report?
help: Describe retries, escalation, quiet periods and what merits an alert.

title: When should a routine stop or be reviewed?
help: Include an expiry, completion condition or review owner so old automations do not linger.

title: What makes an answer easy for you to use?
help: Choose the format you generally prefer.
options: Brief answer first, details when useful

title: What deserves an interruption?
help: Describe genuine urgency, the channel you prefer and situations that should wait.

title: Show or describe a response style that works for you.
help: You can use a short example you wrote; do not paste private correspondence.

title: How should Hermes keep you informed during longer work?
help: Describe useful milestones and how often updates become distracting.

title: How should the voice change for different audiences?
help: Distinguish communication with you from drafts intended for other people.

title: How should setbacks and mistakes be reported?
help: Say what evidence, explanation and proposed next step you need.

title: Would you like creative help in this relationship?
help: A simple starting preference is enough.

title: What makes work feel like yours?
help: Describe qualities to preserve, references you like or things that make work feel generic.

title: What creative outputs do you want help producing?
help: Describe formats, audience and where the work will be used.

title: What should guide your public voice?
help: Describe tone, themes and topics that should be avoided.

title: How should drafts be reviewed before publication?
help: Name the approval owner and what evidence would show the final version is ready.

title: What source material and rights should creative work respect?
help: Describe permitted references and attribution requirements without copying restricted material.

title: How much personal context should Hermes handle?
help: You can keep this entirely work-focused.

title: What personal boundaries should always be respected?
help: Describe categories of information or decisions that should remain private or human-led.

title: What is shared family context, and what belongs to one person?
help: Use roles or nicknames and describe who may see what. Do not include private records.

title: What home-related actions would need separate permission?
help: Distinguish reminders and suggestions from purchases, bookings or device changes.

title: What everyday routines would you like help remembering?
help: Share preferences and reminder needs only; no diagnoses, medication details or health records are needed.

title: What travel preferences should guide research?
help: Describe comfort, pace, accessibility and constraints. Research interest is not permission to book.

title: What proof should Hermes provide before calling a task complete?
help: Give examples of a result you could verify, including when a test or receipt is needed.

title: When should Hermes stop and return control to you?
help: Describe uncertainty, conflicting instructions, unexpected effects or other hard stopping points.

title: What needs a backup before changes, and how should recovery be checked?
help: Describe the owner, location category and proof of recovery without exposing sensitive paths.

title: How should mistakes be corrected and learned from?
help: Describe evidence to preserve, who should be told and which lessons should become reusable guidance.

title: What should a later reviewer be able to reconstruct?
help: Consider sources, approvals, actions, changed files and unresolved questions.

title: What important decision have we not settled?
help: Keep unknowns visible rather than filling them with defaults.
